Qatar GP qualifying is tonight — and the practice sessions gave us a clear picture of who's quickest at Lusail.

Kimi Antonelli topped BOTH FP1 and FP2. In FP2, the 2026 champion set a 1:23.077, with George Russell 0.127 seconds behind in second, Lando Norris third, Oscar Piastri fourth, and Max Verstappen fifth.

Antonelli fastest on a circuit where he's already looked dominant. The question now is whether the qualifying order reflects the practice positions or whether someone finds a tenth somewhere in Q3.

This is it. Hamilton's final two-race push to overhaul Verstappen for the P2 championship position.

The numbers: Verstappen leads 304-267. That's a 37-point gap with just 50 points remaining across Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton needs to outscore Verstappen by roughly 19 points per race — a task that requires near-perfection from him and meaningful trouble for Verstappen.

Verstappen looked P5 in FP2 at Lusail, which offers Hamilton some optimism. But Verstappen has a habit of turning up when it counts. He won Las Vegas three consecutive times. He doesn't do vulnerability well.

Can Hamilton pull it off? The answer comes in the next 48 hours in qualifying and Sunday's race.

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 10:00 AM ET

Sergio Perez's Qatar Grand Prix just got significantly harder before he's even turned a wheel in qualifying.

The five-place grid penalty from the Las Vegas Camara incident will be applied to his race start — meaning whatever position he qualifies tonight, he starts the race five places back. For a driver already struggling for form, it's a significant handicap.

Add in the mandatory 2-stop strategy (Pirelli's 27-lap tyre limit in a 57-lap race) and Perez has a lot of ground to make up under the best circumstances. The Red Bull machinery can be quick, but navigating from deep on the grid through the opening lap chaos at Lusail is a challenge even a veteran struggles with.

stories.title: Mandatory 2-Stop Strategy at Qatar — What the Pirelli Tyre Limit Means

x_posts.label: Post 4A
x_posts.text:
**Window:** 12:00 PM ET
**Character count:** 188

Pirelli's 27-lap tyre limit at Qatar means everyone pits TWICE in the 57-lap race. No single-stop strategy. Undercut, overcut, safety car chaos — it's all in play Sunday. #QatarGP #F1

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 11:00 AM ET

The 2026 Qatar Grand Prix is going to be a strategy puzzle — and the first piece is already locked in.

Pirelli has set a 27-lap maximum tyre stint for Lusail, and the race runs 57 laps. That means every car must make at least two pit stops. No exceptions. The single-stop gamble teams sometimes try to pull off at other circuits is off the table here.

This creates an open strategy canvas where the timing of those two stops becomes everything. An early safety car can flip the entire race. A well-timed overcut can gain two or three places without a single on-track overtake. Teams with strong pit crew execution and good in-race adaptability will have the edge.

For the championship battle, the mandatory 2-stop adds another variable. A slower pit stop, a close call in the box, a tire that doesn't come up to temperature — all of it matters more than usual.

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 7:00 PM ET

264 points each.

George Russell and Lando Norris head into qualifying night at Lusail exactly level on points. In FP2 on Friday, Russell went P2 and Norris P3 — separated by a few hundredths of a second in practice, separated by nothing in the standings.

Fifty points remain across Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The team that scores more of them wins P4 in the 2026 championship. For both Russell at Mercedes and Norris at McLaren, it's a source of genuine pride — a final ranking that signals who performed better in a season already defined by Antonelli's historic championship run.

Watch these two closely this weekend. Neither can afford to give an inch.
